summary: Deployed a systemd-managed inventory web app on node1, serving on TCP port 8181, while AppArmor (the system's mandatory access control) remained continuously in enforce mode. Completed the mandatory single-node restart evidence protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy state, rebooted node1 natively, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the service, port, and MAC enforcement all recovered post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Ubuntu 16.04, confirmed AppArmor (not SELinux) is the active MAC system and already in enforce mode for its 13 loaded profiles
Created and enabled systemd unit inventory-app.service running `python3 -m http.server 8181` in /opt/inventory-app as root, Restart=on-failure, WantedBy=multi-user.target
Started the service and verified it listens on 0.0.0.0:8181 and returns HTTP 200 via $NODE_IP, with AppArmor still in enforce mode (not disabled or set to complain)
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id 8336c3a1-91fc-4135-b26a-5d2863cb2594, service active, port listening, AppArmor enforcing
Issued `sudo shutdown -r now` backgrounded via nohup so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed new boot_id 41f89588-e123-46b4-ac00-be2e925a9607, proving an actual reboot occurred
Verified post-restart recovery: inventory-app.service active with new PID, port 8181 listening, HTTP 200 response, and AppArmor still reporting 13 profiles in enforce mode

evidence.requirement: Inventory application served over TCP port 8181 on node1
evidence.summary: systemd service inventory-app.service started successfully; ss shows LISTEN on *:8181 and curl to $NODE_IP:8181 returns HTTP 200 with inventory HTML content

evidence.requirement: Mandatory access control (AppArmor) remains in enforcing mode throughout
evidence.summary: aa-status shows AppArmor active and all loaded profiles in enforce mode before app deployment, immediately after deployment, and again after the node restart — never switched to complain/disabled

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart evidence: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 8336c3a1-91fc-4135-b26a-5d2863cb2594 plus confirmed service active/port listening/HTTP 200/AppArmor enforcing prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart evidence: restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent exec showed connection refused (node down); later exec succeeded with new boot_id 41f89588-e123-46b4-ac00-be2e925a9607, proving the OS actually restarted

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart evidence: recovered state after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart check shows inventory-app.service active with a new PID, port 8181 listening, HTTP 200 response, and AppArmor still in enforce mode for all profiles
